summary: Quiet period surge: upstream runtimes crash leading to elevated 5xx and error-rate delta
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 23:05 UTC we observed a sharp increase in 5xx errors for a single dedicated customer (Candela Analytics) during a low-traffic window. The api-gateway surfaced repeated 502/503 responses; upstream serving runtimes in the customer's dedicated pool experienced OOM-like exits and NVML GPU resets. Impact: Multiple customer endpoints (chat and embeddings) returned 5xx for ~9 minutes and user-facing retries produced cascading load, increasing overall platform 5xx rate by ~2.3x for that window. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (c-tn-03) in us-east, prod, tenant pinned to redwood-rlhf-7b. Severity/impact: Customer-reported requests failing, elevated error-rate affecting monitoring alerts and SRE paging.

Primary observed symptoms:
- api-gateway error-rate jump from baseline 0.4% to 9.5%
- Upstream runtimes restarted repeatedly (OOM/gpu-reset)
- Autoscaler did not add capacity quickly due to prewarm cooldowns

Initial hypothesis: A quiet-period scheduling event combined with a small but bursty tenant retry pattern caused ephemeral worker overcommit, heating a subset of GPUs and triggering NVML resets and runtime restarts. The apigw then amplified with hedged retries, producing a backpressure loop.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends a flurry of small multi-part chat requests pinned to a dedicated pool during low-traffic window
2) Many requests have short timeouts and trigger client-side retries within 1-2s
3) Autoscaler prewarm cooldown prevents rapid provisioning; existing ephemeral workers are reused, pushing GPU memory fragmentation higher
4) Serving runtime experiences NVML reset / driver-level fault and restarts, returning 5xx to the gateway
5) api-gateway hedged retry policy amplifies the number of in-flight connections and triggers connection queue buildup
logs: [2026-03-13T23:05:12Z] apigw: 502 upstream connect error for tenant=candela tenant_id=tn-03 route=/v1/chat status=502 resp_time=120ms
[2026-03-13T23:05:13Z] runtime-tn-03-2: [nvml] GPU 0: GPU reset detected; pid=8123; reason=unknown
[2026-03-13T23:05:14Z] runtime-tn-03-2: runtime: process exited with code 137 (OOM)
[2026-03-13T23:05:15Z] autoscaler: prewarm_cooldown active for pool c-tn-03; cannot spawn fast enough
[2026-03-13T23:08:00Z] apigw: hedged_retry amplified requests by 2.1x; accept_queue depth=420
investigation_notes: Checked NVML logs on c-tn-03 nodes: several sequential GPU resets (~23:05:12 - 23:06:00 UTC) on two hosts (host-118, host-119)
Heap/metrics inside serving runtime show increasing GPU memory fragmentation and a KV cache churn spike coincident with the burst
Trace of tenant request IDs indicates a tight retry loop from the customer's SDK: client retry interval=1s with no jitter in several clients
Autoscaler logs: scale-up attempts were rate-limited by prewarm policy; last prewarm event was 22:58 and cooldown prevented immediate new prewarms
No recent model rollouts or kernel swaps recorded for the tenant in the 2 hours prior (checked model-sync logs)
Confirmed that kernel/driver version is the standard GA stack (nvidia-driver 535.x, cuda 12.x); no driver upgrades in the last 30 days
comments: Asha Patel (Support): Customer reported increased 5xx and provided sample request IDs. Asked SRE to triage NVML logs (2026-03-13 23:15)
Diego Morales (SRE): Found GPU resets on host-118/119; suspect fragmentation + high ephemeral reuse. Investigating autoscaler timeline (2026-03-13 23:45)
Lindsay Chen (Platform): Observed hedged retry amplification; recommended temporary policy change to lower hedged factor for this pool (2026-03-13 23:55)
Candela Support Contact (Maya Rivers): Confirmed client-side SDK retries — will patch to add exponential backoff and jitter; asked for temporary workaround (2026-03-14 00:10)

Diego Morales (SRE): Applied temporary patch to autoscaler prewarm cooldown for c-tn-03 to allow one immediate prewarm; also reduced hedged retry factor at the apigw rule for tenant (2026-03-14 00:28)
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: reduced apigw hedged-retry multiplier for the dedicated pool and temporarily relaxed prewarm cooldown allowing a fast prewarm. Customer patched their SDK to add jitter/exponential backoff. Post-mitigation monitoring shows 5xx rate returned to baseline within 7 minutes and no further NVML resets observed for the pool. Next steps: (1) SRE to run a controlled load test on a staging replica of c-tn-03 to reproduce fragmentation pattern; (2) Platform to propose permanent hedged-retry tuning and autoscaler policy changes for dedicated pools; (3) Customer success to follow up with Candela to validate restored service.
follow_up_actions: SRE: schedule controlled fragmentation test in staging (owner: Diego Morales)
Platform: review default hedged_retry and prewarm cooldown settings for dedicated pools (owner: Lindsay Chen)
DX: add recommended SDK retry pattern with jitter to customer quickstart (owner: Asha Patel)
Postmortem: draft within 72hrs and link to confluence page for permanent policy changes
